## Summary

The bug was in `src/click/core.py` in the `Group.command()` and `Group.group()` methods. Previously, the code set `kwargs["cls"] = self.command_class` (or `self.group_class`) **before** checking if the decorator was being used without parentheses (i.e., `@grp.command` directly on a function). This caused the subsequent assertion `assert len(args) == 1 and not kwargs` to fail whenever a custom `command_class`/`group_class` was set on the group, because `kwargs` would no longer be empty (it now contained `cls`).

The fix reorders the logic so that the `cls` kwarg is only injected in the `elif` branch — i.e., only when the decorator is being used with arguments/parentheses. When used parameterless (bare function decoration), we skip setting `kwargs["cls"]` and let the assertion pass, then rely on the underlying `command()`/`group()` decorator functions to pick up the class via other means as needed.

This matches the PR description exactly: "reorders the setting of the `kwargs["cls"]` and `assert (len(args) == 1 and not kwargs)` to allow parameterless constructors even when `self.command_class` is defined."

All existing tests pass, and the new regression test `test_custom_command_no_parens` (which specifically tests a custom `Group` subclass with `command_class` set, using the parameterless `@grp.command` decorator) passes correctly.
